purpose: Source for the credential specification emitted by harness init (plan section 10). No secret values. Branch patterns are enforcement configuration, not token permissions.

github_app_installation.procedure: Installation tokens expire after 1 hour; revoke the current token with DELETE /installation/token. The App private key does not expire: rotate by generating a new key before deleting the old one; suspend the installation for an emergency stop. ghs_ tokens are not on the credential revocation API list (S-gh-token-exp).

fine_grained_pat.procedure: Set expires_in (1-366 days; default 30). Revoke by deleting the token, through the credential revocation API (github_pat_ prefix), or by organization owners (org resource owner only).

classic_pat.procedure: Set an expiry (optional for classic PATs; unused tokens are removed after a year). Revoke by deleting the token or through the credential revocation API (ghp_ prefix). Organization owners cannot see or revoke classic PATs in the UI (S-gh-org-pat-review).

oauth_gh_cli.procedure: gh auth logout does not revoke the token. Revoke GitHub CLI access at github.com/settings/applications; this revokes every gh token on all devices. --expiring is a preference, not a guarantee.

github_token.procedure: Created per job; expires when the job finishes or after its maximum lifetime (6 h on GitHub-hosted runners, refresh up to 24 h on self-hosted). No separate revocation procedure is documented.

human_account.procedure: The human's own account credentials; outside the harness. Removing repository write/maintain role or ruleset bypass is the revocation path for integration authority.

none.procedure: No GitHub credential is issued. Model-provider credentials are out of scope for this GitHub matrix (runtime-and-identities.md section F); keep them out of the sandbox environment through a host-side proxy where feasible.

actions_job_binding.environment: a dedicated environment (for example 'harness-projection') referenced only by the projection job
actions_job_binding.applies_when: whenever projection-only runs as a GitHub Actions job (optional idle refresh)
actions_job_binding.deployment_branch_rule: Selected branches and tags = the default branch only, matched against GITHUB_REF (S-gh-actions-environments). The job has only a schedule trigger: 'Scheduled workflows will only run on the default branch' (S-gh-actions-events); no workflow_dispatch, pull_request or pull_request_target trigger, so no one can start it on a candidate ref
actions_job_binding.secret_rule: The projection App key or the classic token limited to Project scopes is stored only as a secret of that environment ('Secrets stored in an environment are only available to workflow jobs that reference the environment', S-gh-actions-environments). The classic 'project' scope reaches every Project the token's owner can access ('Grants read/write access to user and organization projects', S-gh-oauth-scopes), so exposure to candidate code would reach beyond this repository
actions_job_binding.runtime_ref_check: The job refuses to run unless GITHUB_REF is the default branch
actions_job_binding.rerun_rule: The job refuses any run whose github.run_attempt is not 1 (S-gh-actions-contexts); it has no inputs
actions_job_binding.clean_import_rule: The projection job never checks out or imports candidate refs; it reads accepted state only. Any Git operation it performs follows the clean-environment rule of interface publisher, operation publish_candidate (contracts/interfaces.v1.json): no candidate hooks, credential helpers or filters are executed
actions_job_binding.dispatch_exposure: A workflow_dispatch trigger would allow a run on any branch or tag at its last commit (S-gh-actions-events), exposing the token to candidate code; the trigger is therefore forbidden
actions_job_binding.availability: Environments, deployment branches and environment secrets are available for public repositories, and for private repositories only on paid plans (S-gh-actions-environments); otherwise the Actions projection job stays disabled

actions_job_binding.environment: a dedicated environment (for example 'harness-reducer') referenced only by the reducer job
actions_job_binding.applies_when: always (the reducer runs only as an Actions job in this placement)
actions_job_binding.deployment_branch_rule: Selected branches and tags = the default branch only; 'the deployment branch or tag rule is matched against the GITHUB_REF of the workflow run' (S-gh-actions-environments)
actions_job_binding.secret_rule: The App private key is stored only as a secret of that environment: 'Secrets stored in an environment are only available to workflow jobs that reference the environment' (S-gh-actions-environments). Never a repository or organization secret
actions_job_binding.runtime_ref_check: The reducer job also refuses to run unless GITHUB_REF is the default branch and GITHUB_SHA is the pinned reducer revision read from the bound environment's variable (pinned_revision_location; see rerun_rule). This check alone is insufficient, because a dispatched run executes the last commit on the dispatched ref (S-gh-actions-events) and a candidate ref may carry modified code; the environment rule is repository configuration and does not depend on the dispatched code
actions_job_binding.input_rule: Workflow inputs and every github-context value are untrusted data: the reducer reads them as data (for example from an environment variable), parses and validates them against the command schema, and never interpolates them with ${{ }} into run:, action inputs or API calls. 'Before the shell script is run, the expressions inside ${{ }} are evaluated and then substituted', and such values must not 'flow directly into workflows, actions, API calls, or anywhere else where they could be interpreted as executable code' (S-gh-actions-script-injections)
actions_job_binding.dispatcher_rule: The dispatcher is authenticated as github.triggering_actor ('the user that initiated the workflow run') and checked against enrollment in the state branch; github.actor is never used for this, because 'Any workflow re-runs will use the privileges of github.actor, even if the actor initiating the re-run (github.triggering_actor) has different privileges' (S-gh-actions-contexts). An unenrolled dispatcher is refused before any state read with the App token
actions_job_binding.rerun_rule: The job refuses any run whose github.run_attempt is not 1 ('begins at 1 ... and increments with each re-run', S-gh-actions-contexts), because Actions write also covers POST .../actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun, .../rerun-failed-jobs and .../jobs/{job_id}/rerun (S-gh-fgpat). It also refuses any GITHUB_SHA other than the pinned reducer revision, which is read from an environment variable of the bound environment ('Variables stored in an environment are only available to workflow jobs that reference the environment', S-gh-actions-environments) and cross-checked with the reducer revision recorded in the state branch; never from the job's own commit, so a re-run of an old main run cannot pass its own check
actions_job_binding.repin_rule: Human-authorized pin_update: (1) the human updates the pinned-revision environment variable of the bound environment to the new reviewed main SHA; (2) the next dispatch on the default branch is accepted when GITHUB_SHA equals the environment variable and all other rules pass; (3) the reducer's first transition in that run records the new pin in the state branch (interface state-backend, operation record_pin_update, owner P05). The cross-check between the environment variable and the state-branch record tolerates exactly this one-step lag, and only in the direction environment variable newer than state; any other mismatch is refused. Until the human re-pins, every merge to main halts this reducer (liveness, not safety). The operator procedure and the harness doctor check of both locations are P10's deliverable
actions_job_binding.clean_import_rule: Candidate material is imported only through interface publisher, operation publish_candidate (contracts/interfaces.v1.json): a clean, controlled Git environment in which candidate Git hooks, credential helpers and filters are never executed (plan section 4). The reducer job never checks out a candidate ref as its working tree
actions_job_binding.dispatch_exposure: 'Once a workflow has run at least once, you can dispatch it against any branch or tag via the GitHub API or GitHub CLI' and, for workflow_dispatch, GITHUB_SHA is the 'Last commit on the GITHUB_REF branch or tag' (S-gh-actions-events). Without the environment binding, a supervisor (or any holder of Actions write) could dispatch the reducer on an agent/** ref whose non-workflow code is model-produced, and that code would run with the App key: a second state writer
actions_job_binding.availability: Environments, deployment branches and environment secrets are available for public repositories, and for private repositories only on paid plans (S-gh-actions-environments); otherwise this placement is unavailable (DP-07)

The actor depends on DP-01: on an organization repository a dedicated integrator Team whose only member is the accountable human, with no child teams, verified by harness doctor on every run (actor_type Team; S-gh-about-teams, S-gh-rest-teams; U-PM-15, U-PM-18); on a personal repository the repository admin role, held only by the owner (actor_type RepositoryRole; U-PM-01). EXPOSURE: once a human has approved and checks pass, any Contents-write holder can merge with PUT .../pulls/{pull_number}/merge, PUT .../merge-async or POST .../merges (Contents write, no additional permission: S-gh-fgpat, S-gh-rest-pulls). A required approval does not prevent machine merges. A single maintainer also cannot satisfy the approval (S-gh-pr-approve-required) without a bypass. Not recommended

RS-main with 0 approvals and no update restriction. EXPOSURE: Contents write includes the merge endpoints (S-gh-fgpat), so any Contents-write holder can merge any pull request once trusted-CI checks are green; 'no merge authority' (plan section 4, contract 10) would rest on trusted code only. Not recommended

decision_points.interaction: Contents write includes the merge endpoints (S-gh-fgpat), so neither an approval count nor DP-08 stops a machine Contents-write holder from merging an approved, green pull request; only a rule that GitHub applies to the merge itself can. The recommended option uses Restrict updates in a separate ruleset whose only bypass actor is the human integrator. Pull request authors cannot approve their own pull requests (S-gh-pr-approve-required), so a single maintainer uses 0 required approvals on RS-main; independent review is carried by the Remora review packet and the human's merge decision. If P02a shows the update restriction does not block pull-request merges, DP-11 applies. An App approval is not recommended because it would let automation satisfy a human gate.

decision_points.question: If P02a shows that no GitHub-side rule stops a Contents-write identity from merging to main (U-PM-14 or U-PE-08 fails), what applies?

versioning: matrix_version follows semver. Changes made while the P01 candidate is under review (before human acceptance) do not bump the version; the first bump follows human acceptance of P01.
